claim: On 5 August 2010 (around 14:00 local time) a collapse at the San José copper-gold mine near Copiapó, Chile, trapped 33 miners.

sources.title: Smithsonian Magazine — The capsule that saved the Chilean miners

claim: The miners were trapped roughly 700 metres (about 2,300 ft) below the surface.

sources.title: Cronología del milagro en Chile (EJU, Aug 2010) — 'a 700 metros'

claim: The refuge held only very limited emergency food and water, which the men rationed.
note: Do not quote specific ration sizes (e.g. 'two spoonfuls of tuna') without a source.

claim: The mine remained unstable after the collapse, making entry through the mine itself dangerous.
note: Widely reported; add a source before publishing.

claim: On 22 August 2010, day 17, a probe drill reached the men; a note attached to it read 'Estamos bien en el refugio los 33'.

sources.title: Spokesman-Review: 33 miners found alive in Chile after 17 days
13.cl: La nota que cambió la historia

claim: Families gathered and camped outside the mine while they waited.
note: Known as Campamento Esperanza (Camp Hope). Add a source.

claim: Food, water, medicine and communication equipment were sent down through small boreholes.
NASA specialists advised the Chilean government during the rescue (medical, nutritional, psychological, engineering).

sources.title: Smithsonian Magazine (NASA Engineering and Safety Center was called in)

note: Engineering role confirmed; confirm the medical/nutrition/psychological advice with a NASA source.

claim: The Plan B drill (Schramm T130) broke through to the miners on 9 October 2010.

sources.title: Interesting Engineering — Improbable rescue of Los 33

claim: The rescue capsule Fénix 2 ('Phoenix') was built by the Chilean Navy shipyard ASMAR and carried the men up one at a time.

sources.title: CBS News — What's to become of the Fénix 2

claim: The rescue began late on 12 October 2010; the first miner, Florencio Ávalos, reached the surface at 00:10 on 13 October.
The last miner, Luis Urzúa, reached the surface at 21:55 on 13 October 2010. All 33 survived.

sources.title: Western Museum of Mining & Industry — Fénix II

claim: From collapse (5 Aug) to the last rescue (13 Oct) was 69 days.

sources.title: Date arithmetic from F01 and F12
